title: Performance Optimization and Lazy Loading
description: Assess your knowledge on techniques to optimize React app performance including lazy loading and code splitting.

quiz.question: What is the main benefit of lazy loading components in React?
quiz.explanation: Lazy loading delays loading components until they are needed, reducing initial bundle size.

quiz.question: Which React feature allows you to lazy load components?
quiz.explanation: React.lazy() enables components to be loaded lazily when they are rendered.

quiz.question: What is code splitting in React?
options: Dividing code into multiple bundles loaded on demand
quiz.correctAnswer: Dividing code into multiple bundles loaded on demand
quiz.explanation: Code splitting helps load only the necessary code bundles, improving performance.

quiz.question: Which component is used to wrap a lazy-loaded component to show fallback UI while loading?
quiz.explanation: React’s <Suspense> shows fallback content while the lazy component is loading.

quiz.question: What does React.memo() do?
options: Memoizes a functional component to avoid unnecessary re-renders
quiz.correctAnswer: Memoizes a functional component to avoid unnecessary re-renders
quiz.explanation: React.memo() wraps a component to prevent re-rendering if props don’t change.

quiz.question: Which hook helps optimize expensive calculations by memoizing values?
quiz.explanation: useMemo caches the result of a function, avoiding expensive recalculations.

quiz.question: What can cause performance issues due to unnecessary re-renders in React?
options: Passing new object or array literals as props each render
quiz.correctAnswer: Passing new object or array literals as props each render
quiz.explanation: Passing new objects/arrays triggers re-renders because their references change.

quiz.question: Which hook can be used to memoize callback functions to avoid re-creating them on every render?
quiz.explanation: useCallback memoizes functions, preventing them from being recreated unnecessarily.

quiz.question: What is tree shaking in the context of bundlers like Webpack?
quiz.explanation: Tree shaking eliminates dead code to reduce bundle size.

quiz.question: Which of the following is NOT a recommended performance optimization technique in React?
quiz.explanation: State should never be mutated directly; use setState or hooks instead.
